lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم! أَنا إِبراهيم، أَمينُ هَذِهِ المَكتَبَة
lines.english: Peace be upon you! I am Ibrahim, the keeper of this library.
lines.transliteration: as-salaamu alaykum! ana ibraahiim, amiinu haadhihi al-maktaba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في هَذِهِ المَكتَبَة آلافُ الكُتُب. كُلُّ كِتابٍ يَحمِلُ عِلماً
lines.english: In this library there are thousands of books. Every book carries knowledge.
lines.transliteration: fii haadhihi al-maktaba aalaaf al-kutub. kullu kitaabin yahmilu ilman

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لِنَبدَأ بِأَساسِ كُلِّ عِلم — الأَعداد! الكَلِمَةُ الأولى: واحِد
lines.english: Let us begin with the foundation of all knowledge -- numbers! The first word: one.
lines.transliteration: linabda' bi-asaasi kulli ilm — al-a'daad! al-kalimatu al-uulaa: waahid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِثنان — كَما في كِتابَين عَلى الطّاوِلَة
lines.english: Two -- like two books on the table.
lines.transliteration: ithnaan — kamaa fii kitaabayn ala at-taawila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَلاثَة — عَدَدُ الرُّفوفِ أَمامَك
lines.english: Three -- the number of shelves in front of you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنت! لِنَرى كَم تَذكُر
lines.english: Well done! Let us see how much you remember.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً بِعَودَتِك! لِنُكمِل العَدّ
lines.english: Welcome back! Let us continue counting.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَربَعَة — مِثلُ أَربَعِ زَوايا الكِتاب
lines.english: Four -- like the four corners of a book.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: خَمسَة — عَدَدُ أَصابِعِ اليَد الواحِدَة
lines.english: Five -- the number of fingers on one hand.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سِتَّة — عَدَدُ أَيّامِ الدِّراسَة
lines.english: Six -- the number of study days.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَبعَة — عَدَدُ أَيّامِ الأُسبوع
lines.english: Seven -- the number of days in a week.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَيّا نَمتَحِن ما تَعَلَّمت!
lines.english: Let us test what you have learned!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ما شاءَ الله! أَنتَ تَتَقَدَّمُ بِسُرعَة
lines.english: Mashallah! You are progressing quickly.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَمانِيَة — رَقَمٌ جَميل
lines.english: Eight -- a beautiful number.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تِسعَة — قَبلَ العَشَرَة مُباشَرَة
lines.english: Nine -- right before ten.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَشَرَة! أَكمَلتَ العَدّ مِن واحِد إِلى عَشَرَة!
lines.english: Ten! You have completed counting from one to ten!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِمتِحانٌ أَخير لِلأَعداد
lines.english: One final test for the numbers.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً بِكَ في المَكتَبَة. العِلْمُ نور
lines.english: Welcome to the library. Knowledge is light.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَيْفَ يُمْكِنُني مُساعَدَتُك؟
lines.english: How can I help you?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكَلِماتُ العَرَبِيَّةُ تَأتي مِن جُذورٍ ثُلاثِيَّة
lines.english: Arabic words come from three-letter roots.
lines.transliteration: al-kalimāt al-ʿarabiyya taʾtī min judhūr thulāthiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِنْدَنا أَداةٌ رائِعَة لِاسْتِكْشافِ الجُذورِ العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: We have a wonderful tool for exploring Arabic roots.
lines.transliteration: ʿindanā adāt rāʾiʿa li-stikshāf al-judhūr al-ʿarabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِفْتَحْ قائِمَةَ الإيقافِ واخْتَرْ 'أَنْشِطَة' ثُمَّ 'جُذورُ الكَلِمات'
lines.english: Open the pause menu and choose 'Activities' then 'Word Roots'.
lines.transliteration: iftaḥ qāʾimat al-īqāf wa-khtar 'anshiṭa' thumma 'judhūr al-kalimāt'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَعْدادُ أَساسُ الرِّياضِيّات. لِنَبْدَأ
lines.english: Numbers are the foundation of mathematics. Let us begin.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ المَكتَبَةُ عُمْرُها أَكْثَر مِن أَلْف سَنَة
lines.english: This library is more than a thousand years old.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi al-maktaba umruhaa akthar min alf sana

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فيها كُتُب نادِرَة جِدّاً عَن اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: It contains very rare books about the Arabic language.
lines.transliteration: fiihaa kutub naadira jiddan an al-lugha al-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحْتاجُ مُساعَدَةً في تَرتيبِ الكُتُب
lines.english: I need help organizing the books.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل يُمْكِنُكَ تَعَلُّم الأَرقام لِمُساعَدَتي؟
lines.english: Can you learn the numbers to help me?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَكتَبَةُ قُرطُبَة كانَت تَحوي أَربَعمِئَةِ أَلفِ كِتاب
lines.english: The library of Cordoba held 400,000 books
lines.transliteration: maktabat qurtuba kanat tahwi arba'mi'at alf kitab
lines.culturalNote: In the 10th century, Cordoba's library was the largest in Europe. By comparison, the largest monastery library in Christian Europe held about 400 books.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صِناعَةُ الوَرَقِ جاءَت مِن الصّينِ عَبرَ سَمَرقَند
lines.english: Papermaking came from China through Samarkand
lines.transliteration: sina'at al-waraq ja'at min as-sin 'abra samarqand
lines.culturalNote: After the Battle of Talas (751 CE), Arab forces captured Chinese papermakers. Within decades, paper mills spread across the Islamic world, enabling the translation movement.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بَيتُ الحِكمَةِ في بَغداد تَرجَمَ كُنوزَ اليونان
lines.english: The House of Wisdom in Baghdad translated Greek treasures
lines.transliteration: bayt al-hikma fi baghdad tarjama kunuz al-yunan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابنُ الهَيثَم أَسَّسَ عِلمَ البَصَريّات — كِتابُ المَناظِر
lines.english: Ibn al-Haytham founded optics — the Book of Optics
lines.transliteration: ibn al-haytham assasa 'ilm al-basariyyat — kitab al-manazir
lines.culturalNote: Ibn al-Haytham (965-1040 CE) disproved the Greek theory that eyes emit light. His 'Kitab al-Manazir' influenced Roger Bacon and Kepler.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً بِكَ يا طالِبَ المَعرِفَة. العِلمُ نور! اليَومَ سَنَتَعَلَّمُ كَلِماتِ القِراءَة
lines.english: Welcome, seeker of knowledge. Knowledge is light! Today we will learn reading words.
lines.transliteration: ahlan bika ya taalib al-ma'rifa. al-ilmu nuur! al-yawma sanata'allamu kalimaat al-qiraa'a

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كِتاب — هُوَ أَهَمُّ ما صَنَعَهُ الإِنسان. كَلِمَةُ 'كِتاب' مِن جَذرِ ك-ت-ب
lines.english: Kitab — it is the most important thing humanity made. The word 'kitab' from the root k-t-b.
lines.transliteration: kitaab — huwa ahamm maa sana'ahu al-insaan. kalimat 'kitaab' min jadr k-t-b

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مِن نَفسِ الجَذر: كَتَبَ (كَتَبَ)، كاتِب (writer)، مَكتوب (written)، مَكتَبَة (library)
lines.english: From the same root: kataba (wrote), kaatib (writer), maktuub (written), maktaba (library).
lines.transliteration: min nafs al-jadr: kataba, kaatib, maktuub, maktaba
lines.culturalNote: Arabic root system (trilateral roots) means related concepts share the same three core letters. K-T-B produces: kitaab (book), kaatib (writer), maktaba (library), maktub (letter/written), muktatib (student of writing).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا النِّظامُ العَبقَريُّ يَجعَلُ تَعَلُّمَ العَرَبِيَّةِ مَبنِيًّا على أُسُس
lines.english: This genius system makes learning Arabic built on foundations.
lines.transliteration: haadhaa an-nidhaam al-abqariyyu yaj'al ta'allum al-arabiyya mabniyyan ala usus

choices.english: Tell me about the House of Wisdom

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ممتاز! الجَذرُ ع-ل-م: عِلم (knowledge)، عالِم (scholar)، مُعَلِّم (teacher)، تَعَلَّمَ (learned)
lines.english: Excellent! The root '-l-m: ilm (knowledge), aalim (scholar), mu'allim (teacher), ta'allama (learned).
lines.transliteration: mumtaaz! al-jadr '-l-m: ilm, aalim, mu'allim, ta'allama
lines.culturalNote: The root '-L-M appears in over 200 Arabic words. 'Alam' (world/universe), 'ilm' (knowledge), 'ta'lim' (education), 'ulama' (scholars) — all from three letters that suggest apprehension of reality.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَجَذرُ ق-ر-أ: قَرَأَ (read)، قِراءَة (reading)، قُرآن (Quran — that which is recited)
lines.english: And root q-r-': qara'a (read), qiraa'a (reading), Quran (that which is recited).
lines.transliteration: wa jadr q-r-': qara'a, qiraa'a, qur'aan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العِلمُ نور! كُلُّ جَذرٍ كَبَيتٍ مَليءٍ بِالأَثاث — تَعَلَّم البَيتَ تَعرِف الأَثاث
lines.english: Knowledge is light! Each root is like a house full of furniture — learn the house, know the furniture.
lines.transliteration: al-ilmu nuur! kullu jadr kabayt mali' bil-athath — ta'allam al-bayt ta'rif al-athath

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بَيتُ الحِكمَة — أَعظَمُ مُؤَسَّسَةٍ عِلمِيَّة في تاريخِ الإِسلام
lines.english: The House of Wisdom — the greatest scientific institution in Islamic history.
lines.transliteration: bayt al-hikma — a'dhamu mu'assasa ilmiyya fii taariikh al-islaam
lines.culturalNote: Bayt al-Hikma (founded c.830 CE in Baghdad) was the first research institution in history. Scholars from across the world — Muslim, Christian, Jewish, Zoroastrian — translated and created knowledge under one roof.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخَليفَةُ المَأمونُ جَمَعَ فيها عُلَماءَ مِن كُلِّ الأَديانِ وَالأُمَم
lines.english: Caliph al-Ma'mun gathered scholars of all religions and nations within it.
lines.transliteration: al-khalifa al-ma'muun jama'a fiihaa ulamaa' min kull al-adyaan wal-umam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَرجَمَ الحُنَينُ بنُ إِسحاق أَكثَرَ مِن مِئَةِ كِتابٍ يونانيٍّ
lines.english: Hunayn ibn Ishaq translated over 100 Greek books.
lines.transliteration: tarjama al-hunayn ibn ishaaq akthar min mi'at kitaabin yunaaniyy
lines.culturalNote: Hunayn ibn Ishaq (809-873 CE) was a Nestorian Christian who became the chief translator at Bayt al-Hikma. He translated Hippocrates, Galen, and Aristotle. The Abbasid caliphs paid translators by the weight of the books in gold.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العِلمُ نور! وَكانَ بَغدادُ مَنارَةً تَشعُّ بِنورِ المَعرِفَة
lines.english: Knowledge is light! And Baghdad was a lighthouse shining with the light of knowledge.
lines.transliteration: al-ilmu nuur! wa kaana baghdaad manaara tasha'u bi-nuur al-ma'rifa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً وَسَهْلاً! أَنا أَمينَة، الكاتِبَة
lines.english: Welcome! I am Amina, the scribe.
lines.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan! ana amiina, al-kaatiba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَكتُبُ كُلَّ يَومٍ بِأَحبارٍ مُلَوَّنَة. هَل تَعرِفُ الأَلوان بِالعَرَبِيَّة؟
lines.english: I write every day with colored inks. Do you know the colors in Arabic?
lines.transliteration: aktubu kulla yawmin bi-ahbaarin mulawwana. hal ta'rifu al-alwaan bil-arabiyya?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحمَر — لَونُ الحِبرِ الأَوَّل
lines.english: Red -- the color of the first ink.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَزرَق — كَلَونِ السَّماء
lines.english: Blue -- like the color of the sky.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَخضَر — كَأَوراقِ الشَّجَر
lines.english: Green -- like tree leaves.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَميل! لِنَرى إِن كُنتَ تَذكُر
lines.english: Beautiful! Let us see if you remember.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ! عِندي أَلوانٌ جَديدَة لَك
lines.english: You are back! I have new colors for you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَصفَر — كَلَونِ الشَّمسِ المُشرِقَة
lines.english: Yellow -- like the color of the rising sun.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَبيَض — لَونُ الوَرَقِ النَّظيف
lines.english: White -- the color of clean paper.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَسوَد — لَونُ حِبرِ الكِتابَة
lines.english: Black -- the color of writing ink.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ذَهَبِيّ — لَونُ الزَّخارِف عَلى الكُتُب
lines.english: Golden -- the color of decorations on books.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الآن اِمتِحانُ الأَلوان!
lines.english: Now the color test!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الآن سَأُعَلِّمُكَ جُمَلاً مُفيدَة لِلحَياةِ اليَومِيَّة
lines.english: Now I will teach you useful phrases for daily life.
lines.transliteration: al-aan sa-u'allimuka jumalan mufiida lil-hayaati al-yawmiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ما اسمُك — لِلتَّعارُف
lines.english: What is your name -- for introductions.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِسمي — عِندَما تُريدُ أَن تُعَرِّف عَن نَفسِك
lines.english: My name is -- when you want to introduce yourself.
lines.transliteration: ismii — indamaa turiidu an tu'arrif an nafsik

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَيفَ حالُك — لِلسُّؤال عَن الحال
lines.english: How are you -- to ask about someone's state.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! لِنَختَبِر هَذِهِ العِبارات
lines.english: Excellent! Let us test these phrases.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً. الخَطُّ الجَميلُ فَنّ
lines.english: Welcome. Beautiful writing is art.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ماذا تُريد؟
lines.english: What do you want?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكِتابَةُ تَحْتاجُ صَبْراً وَدِقَّة
lines.english: Writing requires patience and precision.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ حَرْف لَهُ شَكْلٌ خاصّ
lines.english: Each letter has its own special form.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخَطُّ العَرَبيُّ لَهُ أَنواعٌ كَثيرَة
lines.english: Arabic calligraphy has many types.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: النَّسْخ، الثُّلُث، الكوفيّ — كُلُّها جَميلَة
lines.english: Naskh, Thuluth, Kufic — all are beautiful.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحْتاجُ مَن يَنْسَخُ هَذِهِ العِبارات
lines.english: I need someone to copy these phrases.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم عَشْرَ عِبارات وَعُدْ إِلَيّ
lines.english: Learn ten phrases and return to me.
lines.transliteration: ta'allam ashr ibaaraat wa ud ilayya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخَطُّ الجَميلُ فَنّ! اليَوم سَأُريكَ أَنواعَ الخُطوطِ السِّتَّة الأَصيلَة
lines.english: Beautiful writing is art! Today I will show you the six authentic calligraphy scripts.
lines.transliteration: al-khat al-jamiil fann! al-yawm sa-uriika anwaa' al-khutut as-sitta al-asiila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: النَّسخُ — الخَطُّ الذي تَقرَأُهُ في القُرآن. واضِحٌ وَمُستَديم
lines.english: Naskh — the script you read in the Quran. Clear and enduring.
lines.transliteration: an-naskhu — al-khat alladhii taqra'uhu fil-qur'aan. waadihun wa mustadiim
lines.culturalNote: Naskh script was standardized in the 10th century and became the basis for modern Arabic printing. Its rounded, connected letters made it ideal for Quran manuscripts.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الثُّلُثُ — الخَطُّ المَلَكيُّ. يُزَيَّنُ بِهِ القِباب وَالمَساجِد
lines.english: Thuluth — the royal script. It decorates domes and mosques.
lines.transliteration: ath-thuluthu — al-khat al-malakiyyu. yuzayyan bihi al-qibab wal-masaajid
lines.culturalNote: Thuluth ('one third') script got its name because one third of each letter slopes. It is the most prestigious script for architectural and ceremonial use, seen on mosques from Istanbul to Cairo.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابنُ مُقلَة — رَحِمَهُ اللَّه — وَضَعَ قانونَ الحَرفِ المُتَناسِب. مَجدٌ أَبَديّ
lines.english: Ibn Muqla — may God have mercy on him — established the law of the proportionate letter. Eternal glory.
lines.transliteration: ibn muqla — rahimahu allaah — wada'a qaanoon al-harf al-mutanaasib. majd abadii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكوفيُّ! الخَطُّ الأَقدَم — مِن مَدينَةِ الكوفَة في العِراق
lines.english: Kufic! The oldest script — from the city of Kufa in Iraq.
lines.transliteration: al-kuufiyyu! al-khat al-aqdam — min madinat al-kuufa fil-iraaq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخُطوطُ الكوفِيَّةُ كالرِّياضِيّات — زَوايا حادَّة وَخُطوطٌ مُستَقيمَة
lines.english: Kufic scripts are like mathematics — sharp angles and straight lines.
lines.transliteration: al-khutut al-kuufiyya kar-riyaadiyyaat — zawaaya haadda wa khutut mustaqiima
lines.culturalNote: Kufic script (7th-11th century CE) is the oldest Arabic calligraphy style. The angular geometric designs were perfect for carving into stone and stamping coins. Early Quran manuscripts used Kufic.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَنماطُ الهَندَسِيَّةُ الإِسلامِيَّةُ تَتَجَنَّبُ تَصويرَ الكائِناتِ الحَيَّة
lines.english: Islamic geometric patterns avoid depicting living beings.
lines.transliteration: al-anmaat al-handasiyya al-islamiyya tatajannab tasweer al-kaa'inaat al-hayya
lines.culturalNote: Islamic art uses geometric patterns, arabesque, and calligraphy instead of figurative art. This led to extraordinary mathematical sophistication — Islamic geometers discovered quasi-crystalline patterns 500 years before Western mathematics.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخَطُّ الجَميلُ فَنّ! تَعَلَّم اللَّونَ وَالخَطَّ مَعاً
lines.english: Beautiful writing is art! Learn color and script together.
lines.transliteration: al-khat al-jamiil fann! ta'allam al-lawn wal-khat ma'an

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخَطُّ الجَميلُ فَنّ! أُريدُ أَن تَعرِفَ ابنَ مُقلَة
lines.english: Beautiful writing is art! I want you to know Ibn Muqla.
lines.transliteration: al-khat al-jamiil fann! uriidu an ta'rifa ibn muqla

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابنُ مُقلَة (٨٨٦-٩٤٠م) كانَ وَزيرَ الخَليفَة — وَأَعظَمَ خَطّاطٍ في التّاريخ
lines.english: Ibn Muqla (886-940 CE) was the Caliph's vizier — and the greatest calligrapher in history.
lines.transliteration: ibn muqla (886-940m) kaana waziir al-khaliifa — wa a'dhama khattaat fis-taariikh
lines.culturalNote: Ibn Muqla served as vizier three times under different Abbasid caliphs. He invented the system of proportional measurement for Arabic letters — using the rhombic dot as the basic unit. Every letter is measured by dots relative to the alif height.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طَوَّرَ نِظامَ النِّقطَة المُعَيَّنَة — وَحَدَّدَ نِسَبَ كُلِّ حَرفٍ بِدِقَّة
lines.english: He developed the rhombic dot system — precisely defining the proportions of each letter.
lines.transliteration: tawwara nidhaam an-niqta al-mu'ayyina — wa haddada nisab kull harf bi-diqqa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَطَعوا يَدَهُ بِسَبَبِ المَؤامَرات — فَكَتَبَ بِيَدِهِ الأُخرى! هَذا هُوَ الفَنّ
lines.english: They cut off his hand due to politics — so he wrote with his other hand! This is art.
lines.transliteration: qata'uu yadahu bisabab al-mu'aamaraat — fa kataba bi-yadihi al-ukhraa! haadhaa huwa al-fann

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا زَين. أَدرُسُ النُّجوم مُنذُ عِشرين سَنَة
lines.english: I am Zain. I have studied the stars for twenty years.
lines.transliteration: ana zayn. adrusu an-nujuum mundhu 'ishriina sana

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبُ أَعطَوا النُّجومَ أَسماءَها
lines.english: The Arabs gave the stars their names.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: النُّجومُ لا تَكذِب! ماذا نَدرُس؟
lines.english: The stars do not lie! What shall we study?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَرقامُ أَساسُ الفَلَك
lines.english: Numbers are the foundation of astronomy.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَجْم — كُلّ نَجم لَهُ اِسم عَرَبي
lines.english: Star — every star has an Arabic name.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَمَر — القَمَرُ يُنير لَيالينا
lines.english: Moon — the moon illuminates our nights.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شَمْس — مَركَزُ كُلّ شَيء
lines.english: Sun — the center of everything.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخوارِزمي اِبتَكَر الجَبر
lines.english: Al-Khwarizmi invented algebra.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "algorithm" جاءَت مِن اِسمِه
lines.english: And the word "algorithm" came from his name.
lines.transliteration: wa kalimat algorithm jaa'at min ismihi

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبُ حَفِظوا عِلمَ اليونان وَزادوا عَلَيه
lines.english: The Arabs preserved Greek science and added to it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اللَّيلَة القَمَر مُكتَمِل!
lines.english: Tonight the moon is full!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحتاجُ مَن يُساعِدُني في رَصد النُّجوم
lines.english: I need someone to help me observe the stars.
lines.transliteration: ahtaaju man yusaa'idunii fii rasd an-nujuum

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ! هُنا أَسماء النُّجوم العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: You're back! Here are Arabic star names.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الدَّبَران — النَّجم البُرتُقالي في الثَّور. بِالإنجليزِيَّة "Aldebaran"
lines.english: Al-Dabaraan — the orange star in Taurus. In English: "Aldebaran".
lines.culturalNote: Over 200 star names in modern astronomy come from Arabic: Aldebaran (الدَّبَران), Betelgeuse (يَد الجَوزاء), Rigel (رِجْل الجَبّار), Deneb (ذَنَب), Altair (الطّائِر). Arab astronomers mapped and named the sky from the 8th century onward.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَ"Betelgeuse" جاءَت مِن "يَد الجَوزاء" — يَد الجَبّار
lines.english: And "Betelgeuse" came from "yad al-jawzaa'" — the giant's hand.
lines.transliteration: wa "Betelgeuse" jaa'at min "yad al-jawzaa'" — yad al-jabbaar

choices.english: The stars speak Arabic! Thank you, Zain.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ يا طالِب! النُّجوم تَنتَظِر دَراسَتَنا
lines.english: You returned, student! The stars await our study.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَبر — اِبتَكَرَه الخَوارِزمي في بَغداد سَنَة ٨٣٠ مِيلادِيَّة
lines.english: Jabr — algebra, invented by al-Khwarizmi in Baghdad in 830 CE.
lines.transliteration: jabr — ibtakarahu al-khawaarizmi fii baghdaad sana 830 miilaadiyya
lines.culturalNote: Al-Khwarizmi's book "Al-Kitab al-Mukhtasar fi Hisab al-Jabr wal-Muqabala" (830 CE) gave us both "algebra" (from al-jabr) and the word "algorithm" (from his Latinized name Algoritmi). His work formed the basis of all modern mathematics.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "algorithm" جاءَت مِن اِسمِه — الخَوارِزمي يُلفَظ بِاللّاتينِيَّة "Algoritmi"
lines.english: "Algorithm" came from his name — al-Khwarizmi was pronounced "Algoritmi" in Latin.
lines.transliteration: wa kalima "algorithm" jaa'at min ismihi — al-khawaarizmi yulafaz bil-laatiiniyya "Algoritmi"

choices.english: Algebra and algorithms! Thank you, Zain.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الإِسطِرلاب — أَداة المُنَجِّمين العَرَب لِقياس النُّجوم
lines.english: Al-Istirllab — the astrolabe, the Arab astronomers' tool for measuring stars.
lines.transliteration: al-istirllab — adaatu al-munajjimiin al-arab liqiyaas an-nujoom
lines.culturalNote: The astrolabe (الإِسطِرلاب, from Greek) was perfected by Arab astronomers. By the 9th century, Muslim scholars had built astrolabes with 1,000+ star positions. It solved problems of time, prayer direction (qibla), and navigation — a pocket-sized computer of the medieval world.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِالإِسطِرلاب يُمكِنُك مَعرِفَة وَقت الصَّلاة أَينَما كُنتَ في العالَم
lines.english: With the astrolabe you can know prayer time wherever you are in the world.
lines.transliteration: bil-istirllab yumkinuka ma'rifat waqt as-salaa aynamaa kunta fil-'aalam

choices.arabic: عِلم وَدين في آنٍ مَعاً! شُكراً زَين
choices.english: Science and faith together! Thank you, Zain.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَقت — هَذِهِ الكَلِمَة مُهِمَّة لِلفَلَكي
lines.english: Waqt — time. This word is essential for the astronomer.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَب قَسَّموا اللَّيل إلى سَاعات وَالسّاعَة إلى دَقائِق — قَبلَ أَوروبّا بِقُرون
lines.english: Arabs divided the night into hours and the hour into minutes — centuries before Europe.
lines.transliteration: al-arab qassamuu al-layl ilaa saa'aat was-saa'a ilaa daqaa'iq — qabl urubbaa bi-quroon

choices.english: Time is a science! Thank you, Zain.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنتَ هُنا أَخيراً! قَليلونَ يَصِلونَ إلى هَذا المَكان
lines.english: You are here at last! Few reach this place.
lines.transliteration: anta hunaa akhiiran! qaliiluna yasiluuna ilaa haadha al-makaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَرشيف يَحتَوي عَلى عُلومِ الأَرقام
lines.english: The archives contain the science of numbers.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تُريدُ أَن تَتَعَلَّمَ العَدّ؟
lines.english: Do you want to learn counting?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَرشيف يَنتَظِرُكَ دائِماً
lines.english: The archives always await you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلّ رَقم لَهُ قِصَّة
lines.english: Every number has a story.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: واحِد — الرَّقم الأَوَّل
lines.english: Waahid — the first number (one).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِثنان — بَعدَ الواحِد
lines.english: Ithnaan — after one (two).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَلاثَة — رَقمٌ مُبارَك
lines.english: Thalaatha — a blessed number (three).
